description: Team Protopulse is a group of passionate builders making space engineering accessible through play. We combine game development, simulation, and UI/UX design to turn complex mission-planning concepts into hands-on experiences. Mission design is just abstract trade-offs until you get to fly the mission yourself. We aim to inspire the next generation of space engineers.
summary: Protopulse is an interactive web game that lets players design, manage, and simulate a complete space mission. Players choose a mission objective (lunar orbiter, Mars rover, or Europa flyby), a launch vehicle, a spacecraft bus, and science instruments. They must stay within limits on budget, mass, power, and communications. When they launch, the game simulates the flight and shows a mission report that explains why the mission succeeded or failed. Heavier instruments need bigger rockets, bigger rockets cost more, and extra power needs a stronger bus, so every choice affects the rest. Students rarely get to experience a full mission from concept to operation, so these trade-offs stay abstract. Protopulse makes them hands-on, replayable, and fun, and it inspires the next generation of space engineers.
details: Protopulse is a browser-based game built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with a canvas for the flight animation. Players pick a mission, rocket, bus, and instruments. Live meters show cost, mass, power, and science return. On launch, the game checks each constraint, simulates the flight path, and adds a reliability roll for the rocket. A mission report lists what passed or failed and why. Benefits: it turns abstract engineering trade-offs into a hands-on, replayable learning tool for students. It is creative because failure is part of the lesson: a mission can fail for budget, mass, power, communications, or launch reasons. Tools used: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, GitHub Pages, and AI assistance for coding.
